audit.whatIsWrong: Roar of the Slayer is called a 'shield-break' in four places — spikes[0] 'E shield-break poke', wants.foe[0] 'free E shield-break poke combo', whys[0] 'E shield-break poke', and early 'his E shreds your shield'.
audit.why: Roar of the Slayer 'fires a short range shockwave that damages and slows and reduces the Armor of the first enemy hit.' It shreds ARMOUR, not shields — and Nasus has no shield for it to break in the first place, so the early-game line describes something that cannot happen. The distinction matters: armour shred stacking with Spirit Fire changes the trade maths, and a player told it breaks shields will misjudge every exchange.
audit.corrected: Roar of the Slayer shreds armour and slows; it does not break shields.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five places claim Wither cancels or whiffs a charging Decimating Smash: spikes[1] 'cancel the Q knockup window', wants.you[1] 'so the knockup whiffs', early 'slap it on mid-charge and his Q whiffs', mid 'ramps his charged Q to a crawl so the knockup never lands', whys[2] 'cancel his charged-Q knockup'.
audit.why: Wither is a slow — 'decelerating their Move Speed and Attack Speed'. A slow does not interrupt a charged ability; Decimating Smash still fires. What Wither genuinely does is stop Sion closing or repositioning, which is what lets you step out of the swing area yourself. Telling a player the charge is cancelled means he will stand still after casting Wither and eat the knockup. This is the same over-claim I found in the Riven entry, where Wither was said to stop her dashes — Nasus's W is being written up as a lockdown rather than a slow across multiple matchups.
audit.corrected: Wither does not cancel the charge; it keeps him from closing so you can walk out of the swing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Glory in Death is referenced only as 'his zombie passive' and 'zombie state', with no statement of what it actually does.
audit.why: 'After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate with rapidly decaying Health. His attacks become very rapid, heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health.' Both flagged interactions in _missing-interactions.json for this matchup live here: needs-antiheal (he heals) and resistances-invalidated (max-health damage). For Nasus specifically this is as bad as it gets — the zombie's damage scales off the exact stat Nasus stacks, and it heals through the grind he is told to commit to. Killing Sion starts a second fight the entry never warns about.
audit.corrected: Glory in Death reanimates him with rapid attacks that heal him and deal bonus damage based on YOUR maximum health — bring Grievous Wounds and disengage from the corpse.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. Confirmed, and breakdown.cooldowns lists Decimating Smash twice with no numbers.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10/9/8/7/6, Soul Furnace 15/14/13/12/11, Roar of the Slayer 12/11/10/9/8. The sequencing line the matchup actually needs is Soul Furnace's: it shields, then 'can reactivate after 3 seconds to deal Magic Damage to enemies nearby' — so there is a fixed three-second timer between the shield going up and the detonation. Waiting that out is a concrete 'wait for X before you Y' rule, and the full layer's dontsFull[1] is even titled 'Fight into his W shield' while its body text is generic boilerplate that never mentions the timer.
audit.corrected: Soul Furnace detonates 3 seconds after the shield goes up — wait it out before committing. Decimating Smash 10s at rank 1, Roar of the Slayer 12s at 800 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The minion-knockback half of Roar of the Slayer is never mentioned.
audit.why: 'If the shockwave hits a minion or monster, it will be knocked back, damaging, slowing, and reducing the Armor of all enemies that it passes through.' Sion can fire it into the wave to send a minion through you, which extends its effective reach and is the main way he pokes a Nasus who is standing behind minions to farm safely. That is exactly the situation this entry tells you to be in.
audit.corrected: He can fire Roar of the Slayer through a minion, knocking it back and carrying the shred and slow through everyone behind it.

edits.before: Sion owns these levels and you just have to eat it — his E shreds your shield and pokes you off the wave while you have no stacks, no Wither, and your Soul Eater lifesteal is still tiny. Do NOT walk into a charged Q; that knockup is a free poke combo and the only thing that turns his sustain-able poke into a real chunk. Last-hit at max range with Q and on E (Spirit Fire) for safe stacks, and respect that he can shove and roam. At level 3 your Wither flips the script on his all-in — slap it on mid-charge and his Q whiffs.
edits.after: Sion owns these levels and you just have to eat it — Roar of the Slayer shreds your ARMOUR, not a shield, and pokes you off the wave while your Soul Eater lifesteal is still tiny. Watch for him firing it through a minion: the minion gets knocked back and carries the shred and the slow through everyone behind it, which is how he reaches you when you hide in the wave. Do NOT walk into a charged Decimating Smash. Last-hit at max range with Q and Spirit Fire, and respect that he can shove and roam.

edits.before: This evens out as your stacks build. Wither is the answer to everything Sion does — it ramps his charged Q to a crawl so the knockup never lands, and it kills his attack speed if he tries to shield-and-swing. At 6 your Fury of the Sands lets you survive or win a single committed all-in, but don't overstay: his charged Q and zombie passive mean an over-extended Nasus still gets collapsed by a gank. Keep farming Q, use Spirit Fire to shred his armor and stack off the wave, and pick the prolonged fights where your lifesteal beats his shields.
edits.after: This evens out as your stacks build, but be precise about what Wither does. It is a slow, so it will not cancel a charging Decimating Smash — the swing still fires. What it does is stop him closing the gap, and that is what lets you walk out of the area. It does gut his attack speed if he shields and swings. Soul Furnace detonates three seconds after the shield goes up, so wait that timer out before you commit. Keep farming Q, and use Spirit Fire to shred his armour and stack off the wave.

edits.before: First item is your cleanest 1v1 window — empowered Q plus Wither plus ult out-grinds his shields, and Soul Eater heals through everything he pokes back. But this is an EVEN lane for a reason: Sion scales tanky and brings real teamfight value with his charged Q knockup and zombie state, so neither of you truly closes the other out solo. Treat it as a splitpush race — your infinite Q wins side lanes, but never facecheck a lane-pushing Sion winding up a wall-pin Q, and let your team punish his immobility while you take towers.
edits.after: First item is your cleanest 1v1 window — empowered Q plus Wither plus ult out-grinds Soul Furnace, and Soul Eater heals through his poke. But killing him does not end it: Glory in Death reanimates him with very rapid attacks that heal him and deal bonus damage off your MAXIMUM health, so the fatter you have built, the harder the corpse hits. Buy Grievous Wounds before you take that duel, and walk away from the zombie instead of trading with it — that health decays on its own.

notes: DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: Unstoppable Onslaught's name and its 'hardCC' flag both suggest Sion is immune to crowd control during the charge, which would mean Wither cannot slow him out of it — a genuinely decisive fact for a Nasus whose only tool is a slow. But nothing in Riot's description in the kit file says he is unstoppable, and the brief tells me not to infer this class of property from the file. I wrote nothing about it either way. Please verify Unstoppable Onslaught's CC-immunity on the Wiki; if Sion is unstoppable during it, this entry needs an explicit line saying Wither will not stop the charge, because the current text encourages exactly that reflex. PROBABLE KIT DATA ARTIFACT: champ-data/_kits/sion.json tags Soul Furnace (W) with the percentHealth flag, but Riot's description only says it 'shields himself... to deal Magic Damage to enemies nearby' plus 'When Sion kills enemies, he passively gains maximum Health'. The flag looks derived from the phrase 'maximum Health' describing Sion's own health gain, not damage dealt to a target. I therefore made no percent-health claim about W and confined that claim to the passive, where Riot's text is explicit ('bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health'). If any generator consumed the W flag, other entries may credit Sion with percent-health damage he does not have. Finally: the Wither over-claim pattern (Riven's dashes, Sion's charge) appears twice in my slice and is worth a global grep — Nasus's W is a slow and is repeatedly written as though it were a root, an interrupt, or a dash-stopper.
